in_book: Fishing royalty. The black lateral stripe is the tell-tale. Matt's 36-inch, 20-pound monster at South Point (Ch. 6).
how_matt_fishes_it: Bagley Mullet lure in moonlight, or a live shrimp on a size-6 hook with a weighted leader, near high tide along mangroves and rocks. Thirty-pound leader. Big snook jump and run for the oysters.
identify: Long body, protruding lower jaw, single black stripe nose to tail.
habitat: Mangrove shorelines, oyster bars, river mouths, passes
regulation_note: Catch-and-release only during the closed season in the book (May–Sept Gulf side). Check current FWC rules.

in_book: The trophy fish of South Florida and the tournament's main event. Old Scarface. Rose's 68-inch, 81-pound winner.
how_matt_fishes_it: Trolling a lure a hundred feet behind the Sea Belle at a river mouth; thick 'boat poles' with 30-lb line. Tarpon leap and shake to throw the hook — bow to the fish, reel on the way down.
identify: Huge silver scales, upturned mouth, long trailing dorsal ray.
habitat: Passes, river mouths, grass flats, open Gulf
regulation_note: Catch-and-release only in Florida; a tag is required to possess one. Weigh-in tournaments like the book's are now mostly measure-and-release.

in_book: The first keeper Matt ever caught, at Comer Key. Rose's cooler-toppling redfish at the marina. The 22- and 24-inch keepers at Lostman's (Ch. 16).
how_matt_fishes_it: Popping cork with a live shrimp over oyster bars on a dropping tide.
identify: Copper-bronze, one or more black spots at the base of the tail.
typical_size: 18–27 in slot; bull reds over 40 in
habitat: Oyster bars, mangrove points, shallow bays
regulation_note: Slot limit and bag limit vary by region; check FWC.

in_book: 'Grass bed fishing meant trout.' Three keepers on the first client trip; Dave's trout off Little Pavilion Key.
how_matt_fishes_it: Jigging a yellow feather tipped with shrimp over grass beds; soft mouth, so don't yank.
identify: Silver-gray with black spots on back, dorsal, and tail; two canine teeth.
regulation_note: Slot and bag limits; check FWC.

in_book: Dave's 22-incher; the snapper bonanza at the river mouth ('leave that snapper in the water, it'll attract more'); Matt's post-storm cooler-fillers.
how_matt_fishes_it: Hook and live shrimp with weight in fast current and deep water near mangrove roots.
identify: Gray-bronze, dark stripe through the eye, reddish tint near the mouth.
habitat: Mangrove roots, river mouths, deep holes
regulation_note: Minimum size and bag limit; check FWC.

in_book: Matt's favorite eating fish. The 'unseen giant' that dragged the anchored Bonefisher across the channel; the one that pulled Doc overboard; the one the gator bit in half.
how_matt_fishes_it: Live bait in deep holes between mangrove islands where the current rushes. Strong arms and back; don't let it get under a rock.
identify: Broad head, huge mouth, mottled brown. Goliaths are the 300-pounders.
regulation_note: Goliath grouper is protected (limited harvest by permit only). Gag has seasons and limits.

in_book: The 'single black drum, which were hard to find these days' in the Rabbit Key cooler. A tournament category.
identify: Deep-bodied, gray-black, chin barbels, vertical bars when young.
typical_size: 14–24 in slot; big ones over 40 lb

in_book: A tournament category at Port of the Everglades.
identify: Long, dark brown, flat head; often mistaken for a shark.
habitat: Open Gulf, around structure and rays

in_book: On Dan's list of what the Ten Thousand Islands offers.
identify: Yellow stripe from nose to a forked yellow tail.

in_book: Matt's metaphor: the tiny ladyfish that minds its own business before the snook gobbles it.
identify: Slender, silver, leaps wildly when hooked.

in_book: On Dan's list.
identify: Flat, both eyes on the left side, three ocellated spots.

in_book: On Dan's list.
identify: Black vertical bars and eerily human-looking teeth.

in_book: 'Those little puffy buggers were tough to unhook.'
'Aggressive jack fish darted frantically under the surface' herding baitfish at South Point.
identify: Blunt head, yellow tail, black spot on the gill cover.

in_book: The baitfish the Bagley Mullet lure imitates. Mullet 'splashing in the current' is part of the Everglades choir.
identify: Blunt nose, silver, jumps for no reason anyone has proven.

in_book: Baitfish fleeing bigger fish at South Point.
The 'spiny catfish' Matt caught as a kid off the Anglers Motel dock.
The fish President Bush hooked with Snapper on the Key Largo flats.
identify: Silver, forked tail, tails in inches of water.

in_book: 'Bleeding like a dang amberjack' — Doc.
The 'giant brim' Russ watches with his grandson off the lake dock up north — about the size of Everglades bait.
The Chokoloskee Gazette article: smuggled exotics destroying local reefs and 'outcompeting' native species.
conservation: Invasive in Florida waters; no bag limit, harvest encouraged.

scientific: Isurus oxyrinchus (as named in the book); more likely a bull shark, Carcharhinus leucas, in those shallows
in_book: Black dorsal fin and red eyes in the lantern light at Comer Key. Dan cuts the line: 'There is such a thing as too much fish.'
Arrives at the ghost net while Matt is freeing the baby dolphin; driven off by the mother dolphin.
